messages:
beth: Heads-up: user reported `pip install redwood-python-sdk[async]` didn't pull `aiohttp` and their app crashed with ModuleNotFoundError. Repro locally with pip 23.3 on macOS.

beth: Repro steps: `pip install redwood-python-sdk[async]` -> `python -c \"import aiohttp\"` -> ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'aiohttp'

sam: That's odd. The extras in pyproject used to be `extras = { 'async-client': ['aiohttp>=3.8'], 'sync': ['requests>=2.28'] }`. Did we switch the extras key to `async` in the code but not in the published wheel?

lee: I inspected the wheel METADATA of the published 0.11.0 on PyPI. In METADATA: `Provides-Extra: async-client` — so the published wheel exposes extras name `async-client` while our README and quickstart ask for `[async]`. Bad mismatch. Likely during a rename in pyproject the manifest ended up different than the release artifacts.

nina: Oof. So users following docs ask for `[async]` but wheel only recognizes `[async-client]`. Pip silently accepts the package install but doesn't install extra deps if you request a non-existent extra. We should either publish a new wheel with extras matching docs or update docs to recommend the actual extra name until release.

sam: Two immediate action items: 1) patch the docs and quickstart to show the exact extra name that matches the latest published wheel (`[async-client]`) so onboarding isn't blocked, 2) rebuild and republish 0.11.1 with corrected pyproject extras mapping so docs can go back to `[async]`.

beth: Agreed. Can we also add a packaging smoke test to release CI that runs `pip install redwood-python-sdk[async]` in a clean venv and asserts `aiohttp` is importable? That would have caught this.

ci-bot: Noted: creating CI task to run extras verification across platforms as part of release pipeline.

lee: Small reproducible check I ran: downloaded wheel file and ran `unzip -p redwood_python_sdk-0.11.0-py3-none-any.whl PKG-INFO | grep \"Provides-Extra\"` -> shows `Provides-Extra: async-client` and no `Provides-Extra: async`. That confirms mismatch at packaging time.

nina: How did this happen? Looking at the release branch history, there was a refactor that renamed the optional dependency group from `async-client` to `async` in pyproject.toml but the setup.cfg used by wheel builder still had the old legacy extras mapping. We must keep a single source of truth.

sam: Fix plan: (A) update pyproject so extras keys are normalized and the wheel builder uses pyproject only (remove duplicate metadata in setup.cfg), (B) add a release CI step that unpacks the generated wheel and verifies extras names match a linting rule against README/CONTRIB, (C) republish patched wheel.

beth: I'll patch the quickstart docs right away to temporarily recommend `pip install redwood-python-sdk[async-client]` and add a warning note. Then I'll open a release PR for the fixed wheel and reference this thread.

devx-bot: Issue created: #600 - packaging extras mismatch (async vs async-client) causing missing optional deps on pip install.

lee: Also add a tiny unit in packaging tests: `python -c \"import importlib.util, pkgutil; print('aiohttp' in {p.name for p in pkgutil.iter_modules()})\"` after installing extras; or simpler assert `import aiohttp`. CI should run this on linux and macos.

sam: Good catch. Put it in the release checklist too. Avoids docs/packaging drift in the future.

beth: PRs: docs fix https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-python-sdk/pull/1988 and republish PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-python-sdk/pull/1989 (WIP). I'll ping when wheels are live. :thumbsup:
